descriptionChirho: To become dim, faint, or weak, used primarily of eyes losing their sight due to age or grief (Gen 27:1; Deut 34:7; Job 17:7; Zech 11:17), but also figuratively of a dimly burning wick not being quenched (Isa 42:4) and of the spirit growing faint with despair (Ezek 21:7). All occurrences in Qal and Piel reflect the same core semantic of diminishing light or vitality. Multilingual glosses uniformly confirm dimness: Arabic kahata/khabaa, German trueb/dim, Korean heuryeojida, Hindi dhundhli, Spanish oscurecerse/desfallecer.
